claim_1.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 43 vaccine recipients on the day of the third vaccination showed 63 inflammatory response genes were up-regulated 24 h after the third vaccination and returned toward day-of-vaccination levels by 72 h after the third vaccination compared to the day of the third vaccination.

sources.quote: SAM (version 3) using the day of the third vaccination as baseline, with an FDR of 1%, was used to identify genes that exhibited a significant change in expression level at 24 h and 72 h after the third vaccination (n = 43 subjects).
These genes are markedly up-regulated 24 h after vaccination; however, by 72 h after vaccination, they resolve to the levels of expression observed on the day of the third vaccination.

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 36 baseline vaccine-naive samples, 39 vaccinated-and-challenged samples at day 5 after challenge, and 12 challenged unvaccinated controls at day 5 after challenge showed distinct global expression patterns, with vaccinated challenged volunteers separating from both baseline and challenged unvaccinated groups.

sources.quote: Red spheres denote 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge (group A). Blue spheres denote 39 volunteers who are vaccinated and then challenged (group B), and green spheres denote 12 control nonvaccinated volunteers who were challenged (group C).

The separation of group A and group B reflects the combined effect of vaccination and challenge. The separation of group A and group C reflects the effects of challenge and challenge only. The separation of group B and group C indicates that volunteers who are vaccinated (group B) respond to challenge differently from those who are not vaccinated (group C).

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 39 vaccine recipients at day 5 after challenge showed a 393-gene classifier sorted protected, delayed-onset, and nonprotected outcome groups with 100% accuracy.

sources.quote: PAM-R was used to identify sets of classifier genes capable of sorting samples (n = 39 subjects) into protected, not protected, and delayed onset of disease categories, on day 5 after challenge.
Figure 3A shows the results of PAM-R for these groups.

Prediction analysis of microarrays with R (PAM-R) classification analysis of outcome at 5 days after challenge. A, PAM-R analysis with 100% accuracy in classification by the 393 genes in the classifier set.

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from 37 vaccine recipients 2 weeks after the third vaccination showed the proteasome degradation gene set was up-regulated in protected individuals compared to nonprotected individuals before challenge.

sources.quote: High-resolution GSEA was used to identify sets of genes that were differentially expressed at 2 weeks after the third vaccination but before challenge (n = 37 subjects).
Figure 4A shows the enrichment of genes in the proteasome degradation pathway that are up-regulated in persons in the protected group.

Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) identification of genes in the immunoproteasome pathway associated with the processing of major histocompatibility complex class 1 peptides and differentially up-regulated in persons protected by RTS,S vaccination

claim_5.claim: Q-PCR analysis of PBMCs from 3 randomly chosen protected and nonprotected vaccine recipients 2 weeks after the third vaccination showed up-regulation of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in protected individuals compared to nonprotected individuals.

sources.quote: To confirm observations from the gene chip data, TaqMan Gene Expression Assays (Applied Biosystems) were used to detect genes in the immunoproteasome pathway (PSME2, PSMB9, PSMB6, and PSMA4) in 3 randomly chosen samples from protected and nonprotected persons, at 2 weeks after the third vaccination.
Reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) confirmation of the up-regulation of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in protected individuals.
Fold change values denoted by triangles are consistently greater than those denoted by stars, confirming the up-regulation of these genes in protected individuals.

claim_6.claim: Q-PCR analysis of PBMCs 2 weeks after the third vaccination showed RT-PCR-based fold changes for PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 correlated with Affymetrix GeneChip-based fold changes, with correlation coefficient r = 0.886.

sources.quote: The correlation coefficient for concordance of these 2 independent techniques was r = 0.886, as shown in Figure 6B.

B, The fold change in gene expression (as shown on the x-axis) detected by RT-PCR and the fold change (as shown on the y-axis) detected by Affymetrix GeneChip technology. The correlation coefficient is 0.886.
